chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no one to whom death presents itself except that Iblees assigns one of his devils to command him to commit disbelief and to make him doubt his religion until his soul departs. So the one who was a believer, he will not have power over him.
Thus when you attend your dying ones, instruct them in the testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His Messenger, until he dies.

And in another narration, he said: Instruct him with the words of relief (kalimat al-faraj) and the two testimonies, and enumerate for him the acknowledgement of the Imams (peace be upon them) one after one, until the speech is cut off from him.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْن: The Two Testimonies — lā ilāha illā Allāh (no god but Allah) and Muhammadun rasūl Allāh (Muhammad is His Messenger)
key_terms.الْإِقْرَار بِالْأَئِمَّة: Acknowledgment of the Imams — the Shia practice of affirming belief in the twelve Imams
key_terms.تَلْقِين: Talqeen — the practice of instructing the dying person to recite the shahada and other formulas of faith
key_terms.كَلِمَاتُ الْفَرَج: Kalimat al-Faraj — 'words of relief', specific Shia supplicatory phrases invoking the names of the Imams and seeking divine relief

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia practice of talqeen at the time of death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) teaches that at the moment of death, Iblees dispatches a devil to cause the dying person to doubt their faith and commit disbelief. However, the devil has no power over true believers. The Imam instructs the community to recite the shahada (declaration of faith) to the dying and, in a second narration, to enumerate the names of the Imams one by one as well as the words of relief (kalimat al-faraj), until the dying person is no longer able to speak. This teaching reflects the intense spiritual battle at the moment of death in Shia theological understanding, and the communal responsibility to protect the faith of the dying.
